newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

MOD officials could be disciplined after a critical report accused them of wrongly advising ministers over the use of organophosphates in the Gulf War. The Armed Forces Minister Nicholas Soames had to apologise to the House of Commons for misleading MPs.
MARKETS WAIT FOR THE WORD FROM GREENSPAN

Alan Greenspan's comments on equity markets rising too fast has put traders on alert for an interest rate change. The chairman of the US Federal Reserve is due to outline economic and monetary policy to Congress today.
C&W TIE-UP TALK WITH DEUTSCHE TELEKOM'
Deutsche Telekom has advised caution over growing speculation of a partnership deal with Cable and Wireless. C&W abandoned its European alliance with Veba earlier in the year.
PARTNERS SET COURSE FOR OFFSHORE SHELTER

Ernst & Young is set to register in Jersey to take advantage of limited liability status despite comments by the President of the Board of Trade that the British government was keen to address the issue. Limited liability partnerships are widely available in the US and elsewhere.
UNLUCKY INTERNET STRIKE FOR BAT ARM

BAT'S tobacco division Brown & Williamson has been criticised for launching a website designed to appeal to young people. The Federal Trade Commission is debating whether marketers should identify themselves in advertising and marketing.
